safety.confidence_note: full text read (PMC5983391). INT-2228 and INT-2231 identified as tropifexor and cilofexor from the chemical names given in Methods.
safety.note: Tropifexor and cilofexor tool batches raised LDL-C and lowered HDL-C in mice with human hepatocyte livers; predicted a class LDL rise.
safety.short: Humanized mice: LDL up as class effect
safety.quote: Treatment with two clinically relevant nonsteroidal FXR agonists elicited similar lipoprotein and hepatic changes in chimeric mice, suggesting that the increase in circulating LDL-C is a class effect of FXR activation.
safety.judgement: Intercept-run model built to reproduce obeticholic acid's human LDL rise (a retrodiction for OCA, which is not a member); for the member drugs it was a prospective class prediction made before their patient lipid data.

safety.confidence_note: patient side full text read by the draft (PMC9941046); year from the FLIGHT-FXR registry results posting (NCT02855164)
safety.note: FLIGHT-FXR: tropifexor raised LDL-C and lowered HDL-C in NASH patients, as the humanized mice predicted.
safety.quote: Tropifexor treatment was associated with an overall trend of increase in low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) and decrease in high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (HDL-C) levels (Extended Data Fig. 2)
safety.judgement: Paired: Sanyal does not cite the PXB study. Same direction for the drug dosed in the mice (INT-2228). Vonafexor (LIVIFY) also raised LDL in patients.

safety.magnitude_basis: LDL-C/HDL-C change with cilofexor vs predicted rise
safety.confidence_note: full text read (PMC10014688). Patel 2020 (hep.31205) reportedly found no LDL-C/HDL-C difference vs placebo in NASH patients, which would date this 2020, but the full text was paywalled and no verbatim sentence could be read.
safety.note: Cilofexor, the other drug dosed in the mice, left LDL, HDL and total cholesterol unchanged in volunteers dosed up to 300 mg.
safety.short: Cilofexor: no lipid change in humans
safety.quote: No clinically relevant changes in 12‐lead ECGs, lipids (total cholesterol, high‐density lipoprotein [HDL], low‐density lipoprotein [LDL], and triglycerides) or vital signs
safety.judgement: One drug's contra beats another's same on the same model: the mice predicted an LDL rise for INT-2231 (cilofexor) and humans showed none. Healthy volunteers, up to 14 days; the mouse dose may exceed human hepatic exposure of an intestine-biased agonist, so a dose mismatch may explain it. Quote is the opening clause of the sentence.

safety.confidence_note: year is a proxy: the screen selected cilofexor before its first-in-human studies (healthy-volunteer abstracts 2016); the model was first described in print in 2024. Abstract-level (PMID 38409114); full text 403.
safety.note: Gilead/Phenex built a high-fat-diet mouse screen on Px-102's human ALT and cholesterol rises; cilofexor was picked for minor changes.
safety.short: Mouse screen built on Px-102 harms
safety.quote: These data guided development of a high fat diet mouse model to screen FXR agonists based on ALT and cholesterol changes. Cilofexor was identified to elicit only minor changes in these parameters.
safety.judgement: Calibrated on a non-member (Px-102) human result, which is a retrodiction for Px-102 and not scored; for cilofexor it was a prospective selection.

safety.magnitude_basis: ALT and cholesterol: minor/none in mice and in phase 1 humans
safety.confidence_note: abstract-level (PMID 38409114; full text 403). Human side corroborated verbatim by Younis 2023 (PMC10014688): no clinically relevant lipid changes in volunteers.
safety.note: The sponsor paper sets the screen's minor ALT/cholesterol call for cilofexor beside its clean phase 1 safety profile.
safety.short: Cilofexor clean in mice and phase 1
safety.quote: Cilofexor demonstrated antisteatotic and antifibrotic efficacy in rodent models and antisteatotic efficacy in a monkey model, with the anticipated PD and a manageable safety profile in human phase I studies.
safety.reason: Minor ALT/lipid change held in humans
safety.judgement: Stated comparison by the sponsor, dated to its 2024 publication since the model was not public earlier. Not a retrodiction for cilofexor: the screen preceded human dosing. One volunteer had an ALT rise leading to discontinuation in Younis 2023, an isolated case; ALT was not raised in NASH patients (ALT fell, Patel 2020 abstract).

considered_not_added: Cynomolgus monkey steatosis model (cilofexor, Hollenback 2024): predicted liver-fat fall; no trial had liver fat as primary for cilofexor (Patel 2020 primary was safety, ATLAS fibrosis); full text unavailable to check PD readouts, so no admissible comparison
Human hepatocyte cultures (CDCA, GW4064 raise LDLR): non-member agonists only

Human genetic FXR loss-of-function or human challenge models: none compared for this class

Healthy-volunteer exposure-response for tropifexor dose escalation (FLIGHT-FXR): a human analysis, not a model system

gaps.lead: Reiberger 2016 Z Gastroenterol abstract (GS-9674 rodent fibrosis model first public)
gaps.detail: Dating of efficacy entry 2 (cdhfd-nitrite-rat-cilofexor): model_first_use_year ~2016, not a retrodiction, year 2020; covered by checker verdict efficacy 2 (corrected, contra 2020) and rule question 4 on abstract admissibility
Strategic development stop, no histology result read out; decision 4 (a stop is not 'failed'), so no model-to-patient comparison and no status change; bdl-rat-cdahfd-mouse-edp305 stays untested
Primary endpoint was safety only; liver-fat fall was secondary, so no efficacy comparison for cdhfd-nitrite-rat-cilofexor (decision 9); patient-trial row only, changes no status
